articles.title: Arsenal 2-1 Chelsea: Gary Neville questions Chelsea's 'all over the place' back three after defeat - but is confident they can finish top three
articles.summary: Chelsea suffered their first defeat under new manager Xabi Alonso, losing 2-1 to Arsenal; Gary Neville was critical of Chelsea's back three - but believes the Blues can finish second or third; Neville: "I'm as positive as I have been for three four five years about Chelsea."
articles.body:
Alonso suffered his first defeat as Chelsea manager at the hands of Premier League champions Arsenal, despite scoring first after just 77 seconds through Morgan Rogers.

Chelsea have now conceded seven goals in three Premier League games - and Neville says the Blues may need to sign more players in their defensive line in order to reach a new level.

He told the Gary Neville Podcast : "The back three, when I watch them, it's almost like their legs aren't connected to their hips and the hips aren't connected to their bodies. It's almost like they're a bit all over the place.

"I look at the sort of best back three probably that I ever saw which was the Juventus and Italy back three with Andrea Barzagli, Leonard Bonnuci and Giorgio Chiellini - three real giants.

"They worked together as a three, they knew how to position themselves, they were great in the air, they knew how to push up and when to drop deeper. They organised the people in front of them.

"Maybe Chelsea will need to actually recruit more players as they move on through the next year or two with Xabi Alonso. He's done a lot already. He's just needs to get a back three that feels solid. They don't look solid, they look like they're a little bit all over the place. So that that's the main thing right now."

Neville did praise the rest of the Chelsea team though - including wing-backs Pedro Neto and Jorell Hato, and says they have a great midfield and forward line if they can keep their key players fit.

As a result, Neville believes Chelsea will at least finish third - and could strive for second place on the basis of their start under Alonso.

"I think they can finish second - third is the absolute lowest I can see Chelsea finishing," said Neville. "So that's really good. If you said that to me a year ago, I couldn't see where this project was going.

"I'm as positive as I have been for three four five years about Chelsea because I think they're going in the right direction. It's not perfect, they were always going to be [against Arsenal]. I wouldn't have expected them to win - but that was as good as I felt they could have done in the game.

"They can go home tonight thinking: 'yeah we can take that confidence out of that defeat'. That doesn't sound right does it, when you're at sort of the elite level?

"But I think that those Chelsea fans over there in the corner of the ground that have travelled from Stamford Bridge will be thinking: 'yeah I can buy into what I'm seeing. I like this.'"

Alonso admitted Chelsea need to find solutions to their defensive problems but stressed that it will take time to develop their solidity having only taken the job in May.

"My priority is to win games. Normally you win games when you don't concede many goals.

"It's something we need to address. We need to be tighter, more clinical, more balanced. But this takes time.

"We wanted to compete, win here. We knew we were not that far but it went their way. We could have scored for 2-1 and you never know what happens.

"The result is the result; I can't argue against that. But we need to take it, not happy. It hurts. Disappointed for sure. This is our first defeat.

"I want to compete in the best possible way to win. Today we didn't want to sit deep from the first minute. We want to be active, protagonists in the pressing. We have done many right things. We need to make it better, learn from them.

"When you play at the top level, we want to be as efficient in all the phases of the game. But this is where we are.

"It's game three or four for us in a new phase starting with Chelsea. I'm pleased with the spirit and attitude of the players. They worked hard."

articles.title: Arsenal 2-1 Chelsea: Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard shine for Gunners
articles.summary: Nine points from three games, one goal conceded and big players stepping up - are Arsenal still ahead of the rest in the race for the Premier League title?
articles.body:
Arsenal shelled out close to £200m on new signings during the summer transfer window but fell short of landing the elite forward they craved.

Former Manchester City goalscorer Julian Alvarez was on their radar but remains at Atletico Madrid, while the Gunners were also interested in Aston Villa 's Morgan Rogers, Paris St-Germain's Bradley Barcola and Vinicius Jr.

While Rogers opted for London rivals Chelsea , Barcola moved to Liverpool and Vinicius Jr has stayed at Real Madrid.

Yet reigning champions Arsenal have started this season as strongly as they finished 2025-26, when they celebrated their first Premier League title for 22 years.

After wins over Coventry City and Aston Villa , they came from behind to beat big-spending Chelsea 2-1 in a thrilling derby on Sunday - thanks to goals from two familiar faces.

Kai Havertz, an Arsenal player since 2023, and Martin Odegaard, who joined in 2021, scored as they passed their first big test of the campaign against opponents who have spent close to £350m since the end of last season.

A maximum nine points from three games, one goal conceded and big players stepping up.

"I can't see anyone stopping Arsenal ," former Premier League winner Chris Sutton told BBC Sport.

Odegaard sinks Chelsea in London derby thriller

Two right-backs in midfield - are Chelsea short despite £349m spent?

Odegaard and Saka star - player ratings for Arsenal v Chelsea

It is surely too early in the season to get carried away, and there are likely to be bigger tests ahead for Mikel Arteta's side.

But Arsenal have set down an early marker as they chase back-to-back Premier League crowns.

Along with Manchester City , they are one of only two clubs with a maximum nine points from three games.

After sweeping aside Coventry on the opening day of the season, they produced a mature performance to come away with all three points at Villa.

Against Chelsea , they had to find a different way to win after £117m signing Rogers fired Chelsea into a second-minute lead.

"Our mentality is to keep fighting. We have shown that many times," said captain Odegaard, who scored the 50th-minute winner after Havertz had equalised before half-time.

"We never want to concede early, but the reaction is top. We got our reward in the end and the response was brilliant.

"We showed our quality with and without the ball and the result reflects that."

Odegaard has scored three goals in four appearances in all competitions this season, after netting only once in 36 last term.

"It was a big game, massive game, tough opponent, and we got there in the end, so brilliant," he said.

Former Manchester United and England player Ashley Young said Odegaard's form will be key for Arsenal this season.

"He's just a joy to watch," Young told BBC Sport.

"He's exciting when he gets on the ball, he's allowing other players to get on the ball.

"The connection down the right side between him, Bukayo Saka and Havertz - it's just good to see when you've got players that know each other and build relationships in that way.

"Riccardo Calafiori has been brilliant from last season. He seems to me like he's the one that's got a free role in the team.

"It was his run, and he played it precisely, for the winning goal. He goes quickly, takes people out of the way. It's just clever. Arsenal deserved all three points."

Havertz said Odegaard was back to his "very best".

"He's an unbelievable player - we have seen that over the last years," said the Germany forward.

"He's going to help us a lot this season."

Sutton said Arsenal are still ahead of the rest, despite their rivals spending hundreds of millions of pounds during the transfer window.

"They're such a powerhouse," said the former Blackburn and England striker.

" Chelsea are a good team, but Arsenal always find a way to win. Can you stop Arsenal ? I don't think they [other Premier League teams] can."

Arsenal have won their opening three games of a top-flight campaign while conceding fewer than two goals (1) for the third time - after 1924-25, when they finished 20th, and 2003-04, when they went the season unbeaten.

They have also won eight league games in a row stretching back to last season.

Having seen off big-spending Chelsea , their next league match is at Sunderland on Saturday.

Before that Arsenal launch their Champions League campaign at Napoli on Wednesday.

Havertz said Arsenal will head to Italy with confidence high with after seeing off his former club Chelsea .

" Chelsea have an amazing squad, but so do we," said Havertz, who scored the winning goal for the Blues against Manchester City in the 2021 Champions League final.

"We knew it was going to be tough. They scored early, so it's not easy for us, but we believed in ourselves and changed the game around."

articles.title: El Real Madrid se queda sin flow
articles.standfirst: Primer 'pinchazo' del curso al no pasar del empate sin goles ante el Eibar en el Di Stéfano
articles.summary: Primer 'pinchazo' del curso al no pasar del empate sin goles ante el Eibar en el Di Stéfano
articles.body: El Real Madrid se quedó sin flow ante el Eibar, equipo rocoso donde los haya cuyo ejercicio de supervivencia en el Di Stéfano se saldó con un empate (0-0) y un punto para cada equipo. Quesada hizo tres cambios respecto al once de los dos últimos partidos, dando sus primeras titularidades a Lakrar, Caruso y Beerensteyn. Las blancas dominaron el choque desde el pitido inicial, lideradas por una Caicedo que juega a otro ritmo. La primera gran ocasión fue para Jacinto, que cabeceó alto un centro de Levels. Luego, una jugada individual de la cafetera no pudo finalizarla Keukelaar en línea de gol por la anticipación de Belem. Más tarde sería Levels quien firmó una gran volea repelida por la manopla de Wellmann. Ni el 73% de posesión, ni el 92% de efectividad en los pases ni los nueve saques de esquina a favor fueron bagaje suficiente para que el Real Madrid encontrara el ansiado gol. Evidenció chispa, velocidad y posibilidad de remate. El descanso llegó con tablas en el marcador y la oportunidad para los técnicos de retocar sus pizarras. El segundo acto fue una continuación del primero. Beerensteyn falló un mano a mano por anticipación de Belem y la meta visitante paró un zurdazo de Keukelaar y un testarazo de Jacinto que bien podrían haber acabado en gol. Incluso salvó un despeje hacia su propia portería de Masegur. Corto de efectivos, Quesada tiró de lo que pudo para la rotación. Entró Angeldahl de primeras y las canteranas debutantes Noe Llamas y Zouhir a falta de un cuarto de hora de acción. El Real Madrid pidió penalti sobre Caicedo y el Eibar roja directa de Zouhir, pero Eugenia Gil, tras revisar en el FVS, denegó ambas peticiones.

articles.title: Four wins in a row, but can it only get better for Hearts?
articles.summary: Hearts move up to second place in the Premiership as new head coach Wouter Vrancken gets to grips with a much-changed squad at Tynecastle.
articles.body:
Sabah Kerjota's 96th-minute winner didn't just give Hearts victory over Dundee, but also meant it was four consecutive league wins.

It was also their 10th consecutive home league victory. In fact, they haven't been beaten at Tynecastle in the league since April 2025.

In this calendar year, they've won 12 of their 13 home league games.

So is Sportsound pundit - and regular Hearts watcher - Allan Preston right, when he says things are only going to get better at Tynecastle?

Braga & Kerjota strike late as Hearts recover to beat Dundee

'It will take four or five years to get where they want'

The arrival of Jamestown Analytics to Scottish football has split opinion. You're either a fully-paid up, laptop-toting devotee, or a data-denying dinosaur.

The fact of the matter is that Hearts were within minutes of their first league title in 60 years last season and are now sitting second after five matches, despite a summer of "doom and gloom" in Gorgie, according to Preston.

That was after head coach Derek McInnes, captain Lawrence Shankland, fan-favourite Cammy Devlin and even vaunted set-piece coach Ross Grant all departed in the wake of the final-day defeat by Celtic.

"The new manager comes in, with difficult Champions League games, and virtually a whole new team," said Preston. "It took time to settle.

"A lot of people made a judgement early on, but they've been proven wrong. The manager has been really good, his substitutions have been wonderful.

"This team will only get better, but the main thing is patience. They were so far ahead of where they wanted to be last season. It'll take three or four or five years to get to where they want to be.

"In my opinion, I think it will work. It's working everywhere else, why won't it work at Hearts?"

How have Hearts replaced former favourites?

As well as the overwhelming evidence of Brighton's rise from League One in England to Europe, there is also the tale of Union Saint-Gilloise (USG).

Since Tony Bloom's investment in 2018, they've enjoyed their own ascent from the second division in Belgium to the Champions League, via a league title in 2025, which ended a 90-year wait for the trophy.

Might it be the same at Hearts with Bloom's backing? Well, the early signs are good despite such a high turnover in the squad.

There was a sticky start with defeats by Sturm Graz and Benfica and the opening weekend collapse against Aberdeen, but players have bedded in, with goalkeeper Beau Reus bringing confidence to the backline.

Laurent Mendy started in the North West Counties League Premier Division with Macclesfield, moved to the National League with Forest Green Rovers, and has now replaced Beni Baningime seamlessly in the Hearts midfield.

Tom Renaud, signed from the third division in France, started brightly and scored against Benfica and Dundee United before an ankle injury halted his progress.

Alexandros Kyziridis departed, sold for good money to Turkey. In stepped Josh McPake, who was playing League One football with Stirling Albion two years ago. He's now in such fine form, a Scotland call-up has been talked about.

Calvin Miller is another who has fitted in well, with four goals already in maroon. Go back to early 2024, he too was in League One with Falkirk.

The goals of Shankland have been harder to replace, but Hearts have looked inward for that. James Wilson barely got a look-in under McInnes and spent the second-half of last season with Tottenham Hotspur's academy side.

Now, he has four goals in his last six games and could add to his solitary Scotland cap this autumn.

Coach Vrancken providing 'great entertainment'

The main thing, of course, is that the head coach has been replaced with very little fuss. It took Hearts a little over a week to appoint Wouter Vrancken after McInnes' departure.

He is getting the best out of members of the squad who played bit-part roles last season, with Blair Spittal going from impact sub to captain in the space of a few months.

As for the 'Jamestown players', the story goes that when sporting director Graeme Jones spoke to his USG counterparts, he was told new players needed six months to bed in.

Kerjota, whose winner against Dundee was his first goal for the club, has finally settled and is pushing for a starting spot.

Winger Rogers Mato, who joined in January but only played once last season, is another who seems to be a real threat off the bench.

Tomas Magnusson, a midfielder signed for around £35,000 last season, attracted interest over the summer and has seen his value sky-rocket in the year he has spent at the club.

That does not mean there won't be players who struggle. Sander Kartum has already moved on for free, Elton Kabangu has not made a matchday squad this season, and record signing Ageu has managed just seven appearances.

But there's been far more hits than misses, and new Vrancken certainly goes into the camp of the former.

"You don't come to watch clean sheets, you come to watch goals, and one thing you're going to get with Hearts is goal at both ends," Preston added.

"I like the way [Vrancken] speaks. He's captured the imagination of the fans, and they're thoroughly behind him after a difficult opening. It's great entertainment."

articles.title: El Sevilla sufre otro lío arbitral
articles.standfirst: Sesma Espinosa mostró la roja directa a Arouna Sangante tras tocar el balón y el VAR no corrigió la decisión
articles.summary: Sesma Espinosa mostró la roja directa a Sangante tras tocar el balón y el VAR no corrigió la decisión
articles.body: La polémica arbitral volvió a cebarse con el Sevilla en su visita al RCDE Stadium. Corría el minuto 55 cuando Edu Expósito le tiró un sombrero a Lucien Agoumé para filtrar un balón a la espalda de la zaga hispalense. En la carrera, Arouna Sangante, que volvía al once, se cruzó de forma providencial rebañando la pelota antes de que Roberto Fernández encarase a Odysseas Vlachodimos. Sin embargo, el colegiado Sesma Espinosa interpretó la acción como falta siendo el último hombre y expulsó al defensa. La indignación en el banquillo del Sevilla fue inmediata, ya que las repeticiones mostraron con claridad cómo Sangante impactó primero en el esférico, pero desde la sala VOR, Trujillo Suárez decidió no advertir al árbitro de campo para revisar la acción en el monitor. Una decisión incomprensible que provocó el enfado de Luis García Plaza, que le supuso recibir tarjeta amarilla. Los blanquirrojos se quedaron en inferioridad numérica por segunda vez en este arranque liguero, tras la roja vista por Kike Salas en la jornada inaugural frente al Rayo Vallecano. Luis García Plaza ya venía muy molesto después de los precedentes de la pasada jornada. Cuestionado por la polémica arbitral tras la jugada del penalti no señalado de Hjulmand sobre Kike Salas ante el Atlético de Madrid, el técnico no se mordió la lengua: "Es penalti. El otro día montaron la que montaron por la expulsión, que quizá no era, así que espero que también saquen en el vídeo de LaLiga esta acción. Ha sido un penalti muy claro. El otro día es una jugada muy rápida, se pita roja y la que se ha montado por eso... que parece que hemos sido los más beneficiados de la historia del fútbol. Espero que pongan ahora que es penalti".

articles.title: La 'revolución' en el once surte efecto y el Almería conquista el derbi
articles.standfirst: Siete cambios en la alineación de García Pimienta que sirven para superar a un Cádiz que sufre su primera derrota
articles.summary: Siete cambios en la alineación de García Pimienta que sirven para superar a un Cádiz que sufre su primera derrota
articles.body: La revolución de García Pimienta, con siete cambios en el once titular, tuvo su efecto y el Almería vuelve a la senda de la victoria tras imponerse en el derbi andaluz al Cádiz, que sufre así su primera derrota después de tres empates seguidos, en un encuentro que dominó durante buena parte y que terminó con susto final. Javi Muñoz, Miguel de la Fuente y Leo Baptistao pusieron el 3-1 antes del descanso, mientras que un gol en propia puerta de Chirino en el último minuto maquilló un resultado que no evitó el triunfo rojiblanco, el segundo consecutivo en casa y el primero después de dos jornadas sin puntuar. Los indálicos volvían a reencontrarse en casa con un estilo reconocible, tratando de generar peligro a través del dominio del balón. Javi Muñoz avisaba en el minuto 11 con un disparo raso dentro del área que Ezkieta repelía con una buena mano. Dos minutos después, el centrocampista, que debutaba como titular con el conjunto indálico, no perdonaba. La jugada nacía en las botas de Andrés Fernández y continuaba con una maravillosa combinación entre Quim, Lelo y Cipenga, que filtraba un pase en profundidad para que Javi Muñoz firmara el 1-0 con un zurdazo imparable. Poco después, Leo Baptistao tendría dos ocasiones dentro del área, pero Ezkieta volvía a resultar providencial y evitaba el segundo. El Cádiz, en cambio, aprovechaba su primer disparo a puerta para empatar a balón parado: Javi Castro ganaba la marca al propio Javi Muñoz y Ely cabeceando un gran córner de Antoñito Cordero desde la esquina para poner el 1-1. Antes del descanso, Cipenga, absolutamente desatado, volvía a probar al meta visitante con un potente disparo. Mejor suerte tendría después, cuando robaba un balón en el centro del campo y galopaba hasta dejar solo a Miguel de la Fuente dentro del área con un pase sensacional que el delantero cruzaba ante la salida de Ezkieta. Incluso hubo tiempo antes de la pausa para que Cipenga completara su triplete de asistencias al servir otro balón dentro del área a Leo Baptistao, que definía con la izquierda por debajo de las piernas del guardameta cadista para firmar el tercer tanto rojiblanco. Celades buscó la reacción con un triple cambio al salir de vestuarios. Y Vladys estuvo a punto de embocar un balón que se le escapó a ras de suelo por muy poco a pase de Borja Vázquez, dos de los recién ingresados. Izeta también pudo recortar distancias con un remate de cabeza picado, absolutamente solo, que no consiguió direccionar hacia la portería de Andrés Fernández. El propio guardameta murciano tuvo que intervenir en la recta final para sacar un balón que se colaba en la portería tras un centro envenenado de Borja Vázquez. Y al final el Cádiz lograría el segundo en el último minuto de partido tras una jugada embarullada dentro del área que terminaba metiéndose Chirino en su propia portería al desviar el remate de Borja. El 3-2 definitivo supone el fin a la mala racha del Almería tras dos jornadas consecutivas sin puntuar.

articles.title: 'I am so sorry': Moroccan World Cup star rushed to hospital with injury so horrific it leaves rival keeper in tears
articles.summary: Football News: Ayoub El Kaabi suffered a horrific leg injury during a match between Olympiacos and Volos, resulting in a tearful reaction from rival goalkeeper Marios Siampanis. The midfielder Jota Silva dedicated a penalty goal to El Kaabi, who may face surgery and a lengthy recovery time. Olympiacos has expressed their support for the injured star.
articles.body: Ayoub El Kaabi was rushed to hospital after suffering a horrific leg injury during Olympiacos' 1-1 draw with Volos on Saturday evening.The Morocco international was challenging for the ball shortly before half-time when his leg became trapped underneath Volos goalkeeper Marios Siampanis during the collision.El Kaabi immediately went down in agony, leaving players from both sides visibly shaken as medical staff rushed onto the pitch.El Kaabi's injury leaves players and goalkeeper in shockEl Kaabi, 33, had raced onto the ball and managed to get a touch before Siampanis reached it.The Volos goalkeeper then landed with his full weight on the striker's leg, which twisted violently underneath him.El Kaabi's screams could be heard as he remained on the turf receiving treatment. The severity of the injury quickly became apparent, leaving Siampanis visibly shaken.The goalkeeper broke down in tears while medical staff attended to the Olympiacos forward, clearly distressed by the accidental collision.Players from both teams were equally stunned. Olympiacos and Volos stars immediately waved frantically for medical assistance and called for the medical team to hurry onto the pitch.After several minutes of treatment, El Kaabi was carried from the pitch on a stretcher to applause from those inside the stadium. Armando Gonzalez came on in his place.The referee awarded Olympiacos a penalty following the incident, with Jota Silva stepping up to convert from the spot.The midfielder dedicated his celebration to El Kaabi, an emotional gesture that reflected the shock among his teammates after seeing the severity of the injury.El Kaabi was then taken to hospital, where he underwent tests to determine the full extent of the damage.Reports in Greece have claimed that he is expected to undergo surgery, while initial medical estimates suggest the striker could be sidelined for six to seven months.That timeline would represent a major blow for both Olympiacos and the Moroccan national team.Siampanis later addressed the incident himself, using his personal Instagram account to apologise directly to El Kaabi.“I am deeply sorry for what happened today, Ayoub,” the goalkeeper wrote, reiterating his deep regret over the devastating collision.Olympiacos also sent a message of support to their striker through the club's official channels.“Ayoub, in this difficult moment, the entire Olympiacos family stands by your side with all our hearts,” the club wrote.“Your strength, passion and fighting spirit have inspired us so many times. Now it’s our turn to send all that strength back to you.”El Kaabi has been a key player for OlympiacosThe injury came during a frustrating night for Olympiacos, who were held to a 1-1 draw by Volos and now sit second in the Greek league behind rivals AEK Athens.El Kaabi has been an important part of the side since joining the Greek giants in 2023, scoring an impressive 82 goals in 139 appearances.His form has also made him a regular presence for Morocco.He was included in Morocco's squad for the World Cup in North America this summer, making one appearance at the tournament.El Kaabi came on as a 70th-minute substitute during Morocco's 4-2 victory over Haiti in Group C.For now, however, football has taken a back seat.The striker faces a lengthy period on the sidelines after an injury that left his teammates and opponents visibly shaken.Siampanis could barely contain his emotions on the pitch and later felt compelled to apologise publicly to the player involved.Olympiacos have made their feelings clear too: they will be behind El Kaabi throughout what could be a six-to-seven-month road back.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Arizona State was leading Morgan State 70-7 heading into the fourth quarter of Saturday's blowout win when the two teams mutually agreed to shorten the fourth quarter to 10 minutes.

Head coach Kenny Dillingham said Morgan State head coach Damon Wilson requested the shortened time and he agreed, though added he didn't even realize it was something that could be done before he was approached by referees regarding the proposal.

"I've never been a part of a game like that. I didn't even know that was legal, but I learned something today," he told reporters . "When he asked to shorten it, I said, 'Whatever he wants, we'll do.'"

articles.title: Man City: Iliman Ndiaye says 'you don't say no' when City want you
articles.summary: New £60m Manchester City signing Iliman Ndiaye says playing in the Champions League is where he belongs.
articles.body:
Iliman Ndiaye says "you don't say no" when Manchester City come calling, and playing in the Champions League is where he belongs.

The 26-year-old could have gone to Tottenham but made a £60m move from Everton to City on transfer deadline day and was thrown straight into the starting XI for his new side in a 1-0 Premier League victory over Coventry at the weekend.

In the final week of the transfer window, it appeared as though Ndiaye would be moving to Spurs after they agreed a deal with Everton , but they were unable to proceed with the move having failed to sell Richarlison.

"There was no stress or panicking," said Ndiaye.

"I always say whatever comes, comes. God decides your future - it is already written.

"I was just being patient and when City came through I was buzzing. It was always going to be City.

"I wanted Champions League and playing at one of the best teams in the world. I am not saying Tottenham is not, but when Manchester City comes through you don't say no.

"It has been a good week for me and topped off with a win."

Despite Everton finishing in the bottom half of the table in his two seasons at the club, Ndiaye became a fans' favourite for his skills on the flanks and scoring 17 goals.

"When I was speaking with my wife, I was telling her that if I had to leave Everton it would be somewhere where I know I would be playing Champions League," he said.

"It was difficult to leave Everton . I created a great connection with the fans and the players there, but we have to move on sometimes and it's how football is."

Fernandez and Ndiaye show signs of promise on Man City debuts

Ndiaye started his professional career in non-league with Boreham Wood before playing only seven miles away from Etihad Stadium at Hyde United seven years ago.

Ndiaye played in the Championship with Sheffield United and had a season at Marseille before joining Everton for £15m in 2024.

Ndiaye said: "I don't really look back. I just look to the future and work hard. I never stop. I just look at the next step and this is a big step to join Manchester City .

"It is one of the biggest clubs in the world. There are world-class players, world-class stadium and the fans are brilliant.

"This is where I think I belong. I have worked hard to get to this point."

articles.title: Marcos Fernández salva un punto con dedicatoria a Ceuta
articles.standfirst: El Espanyol ha empatado en un mal partido de los pericos ante un Sevilla con diez
articles.summary: El Espanyol ha empatado en un mal partido de los pericos ante un Sevilla con diez
articles.body: El Espanyol ha empatado a uno ante el Sevilla en el RCDE Stadium. Los blanquiazules no han podido llevarse un partido que se les ha puesto en primera instancia muy de cara tras la expulsión de Sangante en el minuto 56 del segundo tiempo. Pese a ello, los andaluces se han adelantado en el marcador mediante el tanto de Stassin. Con todo ello, finalmente el Espanyol lo ha empatado en el alargue gracias al estreno goleador de Marcos Fernández. El encuentro ha tenido de todo, expulsiones, goles anulados y un final épico. El primer tiempo del Espanyol ha sido muy malo en lo futbolístico y ha dejado muy poquito. El segundo tiempo, las decisiones arbitrales han tenido efecto en el desarrollo del partido han revolucionado el duelo. La expulsión de Sangante parecía desequilibrar el encuentro a favor del Espanyol. Además, poco después, Omar adelantaba a los pericos en el 62, pero era invalidado. El colegiado del encuentro, Miguel Sesma, anulaba el tanto por un fuera de juego posicional de Roberto Fernández, que interfería en los defensores sevilllistas. Poco después, y con un jugador menos, los de Luis García se adelantaban en el marcador gracias al tanto de Stassin en el 86. Cuando ya parecía que el Sevilla se llevaría los tres puntos y tras nueve minutos de añadido, el Espanyol lo empataba en el 98 mediante un cabezazo en segunda instancia de Marcos Fernández. El futbolista perico, que ha regresado este año al Espanyol tras estar cedido en el Ceuta el curso pasado, ha logrado el que es su primer gol en la máxima categoría. Además, por el vinculo que le une a la ciudad ceutí, donde rindió de maravilla y dejó un gran recuerdo, ha mostrado una camiseta con dedicatoria para la gente de Ceuta en apoyo a todo lo que están sufriendo. articles.body:
The Women's Super League says an investigation is under way after Crystal Palace used four substitution windows in their win over Everton.

A statement says that Palace "breached" the rules, adding that they only permit a maximum of three substitution opportunities per match.

The Eagles made four separate substitutions in the 62nd, 83rd, 90th and 97th minute of Sunday's 1-0 victory at the Borough Sports Ground.

The league confirmed the investigation will involve both clubs and referee body Pro Ref.

WSL rules do not prescribe an automatic punishment but any breach could be referred to an independent tribunal, which has the power to impose sanctions ranging from a warning or fine to a points deduction or other sporting sanction.

Both clubs have been approached for comment.

articles.title: Juan Iglesias: "Incluso el árbitro nos dice que toca el balón"
articles.standfirst: El defensa del Sevilla comentó la expulsión de Arouna Sangante
articles.summary: El defensa del Sevilla comentó la expulsión de Arouna Sangante
articles.body: El Sevilla ha cosechado su primer empate de LaLiga en su visita al Espanyol, después de un partido donde el arbitraje volvió a acaparar los focos. Sangante fue expulsado al inicio de la segunda mitad tras una jugada polémica en la que el VAR decidió no intervenir. Ya en inferioridad numérica, los visitantes se adelantaron con gol de Lucas Stassin y Marcos Fernández empató para los locales en los últimos minutos (1-1). Juan Iglesias atendió a los micrófonos de Movistar LaLiga al término del choque. "Estoy detrás y veo claramente que el primer contacto de Sangante es con el balón, incluso el árbitro nos dice que toca el balón, pero que bueno, que luego puede ser que le da con el pie. Eso ya es una interpretación. La clave es que toca el balón y ahí se tiene que parar la jugada. No ha sido una acción para la expulsión", se quejaba el defensa nervionense. Empate agridulce: "Habíamos hecho algo muy complicado, que era reponernos de una expulsión para mi gusto injusta. Creo que Sangante toca el balón muy claro, yo estaba al lado y lo veo y hasta el mismo árbitro sabe que toca el balón. Él lo ha interpretado de otra manera y no estoy de acuerdo. A partir de ahí felicito al equipo, que durante todo el partido ha hecho un esfuerzo tremendo. Un resultado un poco agridulce, pero el trabajo del equipo un día más es espectacular". Carácter en inferioridad: "Creo que es el ADN que este equipo está trabajando, no dar un balón por perdido, jugar con 10, 11 o 9. Hoy ha sido un ejercicio de demostrarnos que con 10 jugadores somos capaces de haber marcado un gol y estar a punto de habernos llevado la victoria en un campo complicado. Hay que quedarse con eso". Demasiados parones: "Mucho tiempo añadido para mi gusto, creo que estamos haciendo un poco porque el juego se haga rápido, pero luego cinco o seis minutos de revisión de VAR... hay que darle una vuelta a eso y seguir mejorando todos". 7 de 12 puntos: "Magnífico, creo que el equipo está haciendo un trabajo bestial, que estamos haciendo un grupo de mucha gente nueva que nos hemos adaptado muy rápido. Lo bueno es que este equipo tiene mucho margen de mejora todavía y queda mucho por delante para seguir aprendiendo".

articles.title: Juventus message sent by Gatti and Conceicao: ‘Never give in, fight against everyone’
articles.summary: Federico Gatti insists the late Juventus equaliser confirms his ‘history, as I never give in, I fight against everyone and everything,’ while Francisco Conce...
articles.body:
Federico Gatti insists the late Juventus equaliser confirms his 'history, as I never give in, I fight against everyone and everything,' while Francisco Conceicao claims Milan 'did nothing.'

It was a dramatic night in Turin , as Alphadjo Cisse had opened the scoring somewhat against the run of play with a well-taken solo effort, controlling the Samuel Chukwueze cross-field pass and drilling through Pierre Kalulu's legs.

However, after Francisco Conceicao thumped the woodwork, Juve got their late equaliser in stoppages through a Gatti header on the Teun Koopmeiners cross.

TURIN, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 06: Federico Gatti of Juventus celebrates scoring his team's first goal during the Serie A match between Juventus and AC Milan at Allianz Stadium on September 06, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)

When he was celebrating, Gatti screamed into the crowd of Juventus fans "it's always me!"

This might've been a reference to the fact he had also scored for the Bianconeri against Ruben Amorim's Sporting CP here, but also a reaction to being effectively shelved this summer.

Gatti and Conceicao make Juventus statement

TURIN, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 06: Federico Gatti of Juventus scores his team's first goal during the Serie A match between Juventus and AC Milan at Allianz Stadium on September 06, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)

"I'm sorry you are shocked, this is what I've always done in my past," Gatti told DAZN Italia when asked about his impact off the bench.

"This is my history, I have an inner strength, I never give in, I fight against everyone and everything with this level of determination."

There had been reports that Gatti was for sale and would be sent to Napoli, following his old coach Max Allegri, along with potential exits towards the Premier League or Turkish Super Lig.

"Clearly, I'll be honest, this brings a point and enthusiasm, but we need to do a lot more if we want to win these games and aim higher."

TURIN, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 06: Federico Gatti of Juventus celebrates scoring his team's first goal with Kerim Alajbegovic during the Serie A match between Juventus and AC Milan at Allianz Stadium on September 06, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)

This result does confirm the general balance between these two teams, as five of the last six Serie A meetings have ended in stalemates.

It is also notable that both goals came off the bench, with Cisse and Gatti making an impact as substitutes.

"During the 90 minutes, I feel the truth is that we deserved to win the game," Conceicao told DAZN Italia.

"Milan scored the goal, but did absolutely nothing else. I hit the post, Fede scored, so it was in a way good that we didn't lose, but we deserved all three points."

TURIN, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 06: Alexis Saelemaekers of Milan is challenged by Francisco Conceicao of Juventus during the Serie A match between Juventus and AC Milan at Allianz Stadium on September 06, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)

Conceicao was named Serie A Player of the Match despite not finding the back of the net, as he has rattled the frame of the goal twice this season.

"I have been working on my finishing, but I hit the woodwork twice this season, I know if those shots were a few centimetres the other way, people would say now I'm a great hitman. I know, this is football, I am working to make the difference with those 5-10 centimetres and get it into the net."

articles.title: Una máquina de marcar
articles.standfirst: El Barça ofrece un poder ofensivo descomunal en este comienzo de Liga
articles.summary: El Barça ofrece un poder ofensivo descomunal en este comienzo de Liga
articles.body: El Barcelona consiguió un triunfo brillante y merecido en Valencia. Y lo hizo exhibiendo un poder goleador extraordinario. Los azulgranas anotaron cinco goles, pero pudieron ser muchos más porque Dimitrievski hizo un gran partido. Este comienzo goleador es el mejor de los últimos cuatro años con Xavi y Flick en el banquillo. Nunca habían conseguido tantos goles en las cuatro primeras jornadas de Liga. En total, suma 17 tantos en estos cuatro partidos, lo que supone una media de más de cuatro goles por partido. Nadie es capaz de llevar un ritmo ofensivo como el de los azulgranas. En Valencia, Lamine Yamal fue el gran protagonista. El delantero está mejorando su nivel partido a partido. Le costó un poco arrancar, sobre todo en ese primer partido en Elche, en el que fue sustituido en la segunda mitad y sus gestos en el banquillo demostraban su enfado. Sin embargo, a partir de ese momento, su mejora ha sido constante. No solo en sus números, sino también en su aportación global al equipo. Lamine va de doblete en doblete. Frente al Rayo ya marcó dos goles el pasado lunes y en Mestalla ha repetido con otros dos. En Valencia comenzó pronto, porque a los seis minutos ya había perforado la portería valenciana. Y cuatro minutos después marcó otro, aunque este fue anulado por fuera de juego, por milímetros. Su segundo tanto llegó en la segunda mitad, demostrando que está con el olfato goleador afinado. Pero Lamine no fue el único. Fermín estuvo a un nivel muy alto, consiguiendo un gol y dando dos asistencias. Raphinha, por su parte, no faltó a su cita con el gol. Fermín se lo puso en bandeja. El brasileño es el único jugador que ha marcado en las cuatro jornadas disputadas. Si se podía temer que esta temporada iba a faltar el gol en el Barcelona, se equivocaba. Solo hay que ver el comienzo que ha tenido el equipo. «Este año no va a faltar el gol», dijo Pedri.

articles.title: Barcelona hit five at Valencia as Juventus snatch draw with AC Milan
articles.summary: Lamine Yamal scored twice as Barcelona opened up a three-point gap at the top of LaLiga by thumping Valencia 5-0 at the Mestalla. Barca were looking to take...
articles.body:
Lamine Yamal scored twice as Barcelona opened up a three-point gap at the top of LaLiga by thumping Valencia 5-0 at the Mestalla.

Barca were looking to take advantage of Real Madrid slipping to defeat on Friday night and they did so in style, sending out a strong statement.

Yamal bagged a double and had a third disallowed, with Fermin Lopez, Raphinha and Pedri also on the scoresheet as Hansi Flick's side ran riot.

Sevilla were denied a win at Espanyol as Marcos Fernandez's goal in the eighth minute of added time earned a 1-1 draw.

After Arouna Sangante saw red in the 56th minute, it looked like the visitors were going to steal the win when Lucas Stassin scored in the 85th minute.

But they could not hold on as Fernandez struck at the death.

Federico Gatti scored deep into stoppage time as Juventus snatched a late 1-1 draw with AC Milan at the Allianz Stadium.

Both teams had won their games coming into the contest and it looked like Ruben Amorim's Milan would continue their streak when Alphadjo Cisse put the visitors in front in the 69th minute.

Juventus got their deserved equaliser two minutes into stoppage time courtesy of Gatti's header which ensured both teams continued their unbeaten starts to the season.

Lassine Sinayoko's hat-trick earned Paris FC a dramatic 3-2 win against Marseille in Ligue 1.

After opening the scoring in the first minute, he then restored his side's lead 18 minutes later following Amine Gouiri's leveller for the hosts.

Gouiri equalised again eight minutes after the restart, but Sinayoko took home the match ball when he converted an 86th-minute penalty.

articles.title: La Fiorentina destituye a Grosso
articles.standfirst: El equipo de Manstantuono perdió los tres primeros partidos de liga
articles.summary: El equipo de Manstantuono perdió los tres primeros partidos de liga
articles.body: La Fiorentina destituyó este domingo a Fabio Grosso como entrenador después de un inicio de temporada marcado por las tres derrotas consecutivas en las tres primeras jornadas de la Serie A, según informó el club 'viola'. Grosso, campeón del mundo con Italia en 2006, asumió el puesto tras la salida de Paolo Vanoli, que había conseguido la permanencia del Fiorentina después de hacerse cargo del equipo a mitad de la pasada temporada. El técnico no pudo sumar ningún punto en las tres primeras jornadas de Serie A. El Fiorentina perdió por 4-0 ante el Roma en su estreno en el Estadio Olímpico romano, antes de caer en casa por 0-3 frente al Frosinone, recién ascendido a la máxima categoría italiana, el día que el club festejó su centenario. La crisis se agravó con la tercera derrota este sábado ante el Torino, que se impuso por 1-2 en el estadio Artemio Franchi. El equipo de Grosso cerró así las tres primeras jornadas con nueve goles encajados y solo uno marcado. El exjugador inició su carrera como entrenador en las categorías inferiores del Juventus y posteriormente dirigió, entre otros, al Bari, Olympique de Lyon, Frosinone y Sassuolo. Con estos dos últimos equipos logró sendos ascensos a la Serie A. El Fiorentina no ha informado todavía quién se hará cargo del equipo.

articles.summary: Los nervionenses jugaron con uno menos tras la expulsión de Sangante en el minuto 55
articles.body: Los fichajes ilusionan, los análisis entretienen, pero el fútbol vuelve a poner la verdad sobre el césped cuando el mercado se cierra. Espanyol y Sevilla se repartieron los puntos en un partido de ‘su liga’. Un encuentro que tuvo un expulsado (Sangante), un gol anulado a El Hilali, un centenario, el de Manolo González, y dos tantos a partir del minuto 85 que sí subieron al marcador. Justo 0-0 en una primera parte con ritmo, pero sin peligro. Odysseas estrenó los guantes para desviar de puños el disparo de falta de Javi Hernández. Kochorashvili había visto la amarilla por derribar a Calatrava cerca del área sevillista. Y solo habían pasado dos minutos. Tenía que tener cuidado el georgiano. Sangante se anticipó a Roberto para bloquear su disparo, aunque el delantero del Espanyol estaba en fuera de juego y el árbitro lo señaló. Dolan se encontró con Kochorashvili cuando conducía una contra y el público pitó pidiendo la segunda, pero el árbitro no le había cogido la matrícula. Tiempo también para el aplauso en recuerdo de Antonio Puerta y Dani Jarque. Ejuke y Miguel Sierra intercambiaron las bandas. García Plaza buscaba algo más mientras el Espanyol perdía esa “finura” con el balón que Manolo había reclamado en la previa. Al Sevilla, eso sí, le seguía faltando colmillo. El nigeriano lo intentó por su cuenta. Arrancó, regateó y se metió en el área, pero la acción no tuvo continuidad. Al menos, dejó un córner. Más cerca del susto estuvo el Espanyol por culpa de su propio portero. Dmitrovic se complicó la vida, salió del área y se deshizo de Ure, que no paraba quieto aunque seguía sin encontrar una situación clara de gol. Guridi no llegó al balón y este terminó en los pies de Miguel Sierra, que probó suerte desde lejos. Dolan respondió con un centro chut que no sorprendió a Odysseas. En la banda, calentaban Fofana y Stassin. La primera parte tuvo ritmo y la segunda, polémica. El árbitro expulsó a Sangante tras una entrada por detrás a Roberto cuando estaba a punto de adentrarse en el área. García Plaza se desgañitaba diciendo que había tocado balón. Tras consultarlo con la sala VOR, Sesma Espinosa mantuvo el castigo. Pero el Sevilla no se arrugó, ni mucho menos. Marcó El Hilali, pero fue anulado por fuera de juego posicional de Marcos González. Después lo compensaría con creces. Stassin, efectividad máxima, remató de primeras tras un potente saque de banda de Carmona y un rechace para el 0-1. Debutaba el belga, uno de los fichajes de José Ignacio Navarro en el último día de mercado. En el minuto 98 empataría Marcos Fernández con una decidatoria muy especial: "Ceuta no se vende, Ceuta se defiende". Pues eso.

articles.title: How Arsenal Nearly Missed Out on Legendary Striker Ted Drake
articles.summary: As many know who read the greatest Gunners platform, Just Arsenal, Ted Drake is one of our greatest strikers of all time and is my great-grandfather, who I m...
articles.body:
As many know who read the greatest Gunners platform, Just Arsenal, Ted Drake is one of our greatest strikers of all time and is my great-grandfather, who I managed to have a remembrance plaque erected for.

However, his move to Arsenal was a miracle and could've easily not happened, which sounds crazy to even consider, but that's the truth according to historical sources.

Drake was born down Holyrood in Southampton, which is one of the most recognisable streets in the city's history. His mum was a landlady at a pub on the main high street and his dad was once a fireman, then a sea merchant, who he hardly saw.

The family received the occasional postcard from him containing his usual slightly comedic message, "from me to you Eli", whilst his mum was running around after lodgers trying to make them welcome, amongst looking after many children of her own at the same time.

A Young Ted Drake Dreams of Playing Football

When Ted was younger, he used to keenly watch Southampton play at the old Dell before Saints moved to St Mary's just over 20 years ago.

He took inspiration from their key striker at the time, Billy Rawlings, who was a local folklore hero and reigning top goalscorer for eight out of nine seasons between 1921 and 1928.

The young Drake dreamt of becoming the first Southampton-born individual to play for his country, England, which he did, scoring six times in five appearances during the 1930s and famously featuring in the brutal Battle of Highbury in 1934 , witnessing the Three Lions win 3-2 versus the World Cup winners Italy at the time.

The future Arsenal talisman would end up joining his boyhood club in 1931 after signing from non-league side Winchester City.

When Ted signed for Saints, he was able to drop his daytime job of being a gas inspector at Southampton Gas and Coke Company, now a professional footballer.

His ambitions were starting to turn into a real-life reality and, for the next two seasons, he was Southampton's key talisman, taking over from his maestro Rawlings, who switched to Manchester United in 1928.

Highbury 1935. (L-R): Wilf Copping, Cliff Bastin, Eddie Hapgood, Ted Drake, George Male. (Photo by J.A Hampton/Topical Press Agency/Getty Images)

During this time, when Saints were in the Second Division, the south coast side were struggling for cash.

In the 1932/33 season, The Arsenal came calling whilst on their way to an eventual hat-trick of League titles, which they haven't eclipsed since (1935). However, Ted refused to bargain with the greatest club in the land at the time.

At heart, Ted was a Saint in the footballing sense, although, as local folklore says, during his local community cricket days he smashed a ball from Hogs Park over the road, hitting the tip of St Mary's Church, which apparently no one has done since or come close to.

I only found this out during my time at uni in the city when speaking to a local lecturer who had grown up playing cricket within the city walls.

In March 1934, The Arsenal came calling for him again and, with Saints desperate for money, gave in, selling the player who was described at the time as "the best centre forward in the world" for £6,500, which today couldn't even buy you a mortgage for a decent-sized one-bedroom apartment.

The Hampshire Advertiser, which ceased to exist in 1940, said: "Ted Drake at the centre of a controversial storm".

The opening lines read from Saturday 17th March 1934: "has been the most talked about footballer in England this week. Few young players have risen so rapidly into the public eye. He is yet only 21 years of age, and is in only second full season as a professional", putting things into perspective.

Drake made his final Southampton appearance versus Brentford on March 10th during a 0-0 draw which attracted 10,439 people to the game. The next home contest versus Manchester United saw less than half that figure turn up for the occasion (4,900).

Drake also explained in the Daily Echo that he didn't really want to leave and felt guilty in doing so due to his strong love for his home place.

Whilst being interviewed at the Dell in his later years, he told the cameras: "I'm always happy when I know I have to come down to Southampton, whether I've got to come down and meet my family, but it's always nice to come back here, there's always been a saying since I was a little boy, 'once a Saint always a Saint' and I shall remain a Saint for the rest of my days".

"I was born in Holyrood and I served my time at the gas company, so I am a real local if anyone's a local I am, yes…"

It's crazy to think that one of Arsenal's all-time greats, who holds the record for the most goals scored in an English top-flight game of football (7) and highest number of strikes achieved in a season (44) , came so close to not signing for the Gunners.

How differently might Arsenal's history have looked if Ted Drake had turned the club down for a second time?

Where does Drake rank among Arsenal's greatest-ever strikers, and do you enjoy hearing these stories about the Gunners' history?

articles.title: El Cacereño resistió el empuje del filial y se llevó un punto de Riazor
articles.standfirst: Rubén López, con un golazo por la escuadra, igualó el marcador en la segunda mitad en el estreno del Fabril como local en Primera Federación
articles.summary: Rubén López, con un golazo por la escuadra, igualó el marcador en la segunda mitad en el estreno del Fabril como local en Primera Federación
articles.body: El filial del Deportivo de la Coruña y el CP Cacereño firmaron tablas (1-1) en la segunda jornada del Grupo 1 de la Primera Federación, en un choque que se decidió en apenas media hora de juego repartida entre el tramo final del primer tiempo y el arranque del segundo. Un tempranero gol visitante y la reacción local nada más regresar de vestuarios dibujaron un empate que deja sensaciones agridulces en ambos banquillos. FICHA TÉCNICA 1 - Fabril: Álex Marqués; Quique Teijo, Samu Fernández, Manu Serrano (Ferrán Seco, min 19), Iker Vidal; Koke San José (Yayo, min 76), Rubén López; Adrián Guerrero (Domínguez, min 63), Álvaro Fraga (Mauro Valeiro, min 76); Kevin Sánchez y Martín Ochoa (Justino, min 63). 1 - Cacereño: Diego Nieves; Sergi López, Expósito (Iván Fernández, min 70), Martínez, Molina; Navarro, Gete, Nico Conesa (Toño Calvo, min 46), Tellechea (Sevila, min 58); Artola (José González, min 81) y Osama (Runy, min 70). Goles: 0-1, min 16: Tellechea; 1-1, min 50: Rubén López. Árbitro: Francisco Crespo Puente (comité cántabro). Amonestó a Álvaro Fraga por los locales; y a Nico Conesa en los visitantes. Incidencias: Segunda jornada de Liga ante 1.086 espectadores en Abanca Riazor. Un guion que se torció pronto para los locales El Cacereño llegó al partido con la lección aprendida y golpeó primero. En el minuto 17, Ignacio Tellechea culminó una jugada asistida por Sergio Navarro para adelantar a los extremeños y silenciar al Fabril, que apenas había tenido tiempo de asentarse. El 0-1 obligó a los coruñeses a rehacer sus planes casi desde el inicio. Y lo hicieron a la fuerza. Dos minutos después de encajar, en el 19, el técnico local se vio obligado a mover el banquillo por necesidad: Manuel Serrano Salazar cayó lesionado y dejó su sitio a Ferran Seco. Fue el primero de una serie de contratiempos físicos que condicionaron el desarrollo del encuentro para el conjunto blanquiazul, dispuesto en un 4-2-3-1 y con Rubén López portando el brazalete de capitán. Con el marcador en contra, el Fabril se marchó al descanso por debajo (0-1), consciente de que el segundo tiempo exigía una reacción inmediata. La respuesta llegó nada más volver del túnel No tardó en producirse. En el minuto 51, apenas seis después de la reanudación, Rubén López transformó el empate a pase de Kevin Sánchez para poner el 1-1 y devolver la fe a la grada local. El tanto del capitán, además de valer un punto, premió la insistencia de un equipo que se había visto contra las cuerdas durante buena parte de la primera mitad. El empate abrió una fase de tanteo en la que ambos entrenadores recurrieron al banquillo. El Cacereño, que ya había refrescado el ataque en el descanso con la entrada de Toño Calvo por Nico Conesa —amonestado tempranamente, en el minuto 3—, fue retirando a piezas clave: Marcos Sevila relevó al goleador Tellechea en el 59, y más tarde entraron Iván Fernández Tamayo, Runy y José González. El Fabril, por su parte, siguió lastrado por los problemas físicos y realizó otro cambio forzado en el minuto 63, cuando David Domínguez sustituyó a Adrián Guerrero por lesión, en el mismo movimiento en el que Justino Barbosa entró por Martin Ochoa. El tramo final, con Mauro Valeiro y Yayo González aportando piernas frescas por parte local, no alteró el electrónico. El acta reflejó también la amarilla que vio Álvaro Fraga Mesía en el 57. Ninguno de los dos porteros, Alejandro Marqués en el Fabril y el veterano Diego Nieves en el Cacereño, se vio superado de nuevo, y el 1-1 resistió hasta el pitido final. Lo que dice la clasificación El reparto de puntos tiene lecturas muy distintas según el lado del vestuario. El Cacereño se mantiene en la zona noble del Grupo 1: es sexto con 4 puntos, fruto de una victoria y este empate, sin conocer todavía la derrota en dos jornadas (1-1 de balance con dos goles a favor y uno en contra). Sigue instalado entre los equipos que apuntan alto en un arranque de temporada donde el pelotón está muy comprimido: hasta seis conjuntos suman esos mismos 4 puntos. Para el Deportivo Fabril, en cambio, el punto sabe a poco. Los coruñeses son decimoquintos, con un solo punto en su casillero (un empate y una derrota) y un gol a favor por dos en contra. En un grupo donde la cabeza la comandan Real Unión Club, Pontevedra CF y UD Logroñés con pleno de 6 puntos, el filial deportivista necesita empezar a sumar de tres para no descolgarse de la zona media. El empate frena la sangría, pero el once de La Coruña todavía busca su primera victoria del curso. Nombres propios El gran protagonista local fue Rubén López. El capitán no solo marcó el gol del empate en el 51, sino que ejerció de líder en el momento en que su equipo más lo necesitaba, con el marcador en contra y el banquillo desarbolado por las lesiones. Su conexión con Kevin Sánchez, autor de la asistencia, fue la vía por la que el Fabril encontró vida. En el bando visitante, la firma del partido llevó el nombre de Ignacio Tellechea. El centrocampista, uno de los futbolistas de mayor recorrido del plantel extremeño, resolvió con criterio el pase de Sergio Navarro para adelantar a los suyos y estuvo cerca de darle la victoria a un Cacereño que se replegó bien tras el descanso. Su sustitución en el 59 fue una decisión de gestión de esfuerzos que, sin embargo, coincidió con la pérdida de mordiente ofensiva visitante. Conclusión El 1-1 entre Deportivo Fabril y CP Cacereño refleja fielmente lo visto: un Cacereño más eficaz en la primera mitad y un Fabril que, pese a las adversidades físicas, tuvo el carácter de reaccionar de inmediato tras el intermedio. Los extremeños prolongan su buen inicio y siguen sin perder; los coruñeses, todavía sin ganar, se agarran a la reacción de su capitán como punto de partida para enderezar el rumbo. Con el grupo tan apretado en estas primeras jornadas, cada punto empieza a pesar, y ambos saldrán a por los tres en la próxima cita.

articles.title: Pedro Benito abre el cerrojo visitante
articles.standfirst: Un centro de Oier que cabeceó el gaditano, al que anularon otro golazo, da el triunfo a una Cultural sólida y dominadora ante un Mérida que jugó desde el minuto 72 con 10
articles.summary: Un centro de Oier que cabeceó el gaditano, al que anularon otro golazo, da el triunfo a una Cultural sólida y dominadora ante un Mérida que jugó desde el minuto 72 con 10
articles.body: La Cultural Leonesa se impone 1-0 al Mérida AD en una tarde de tensión, calor y un desenlace decidido por un solo golpe en la hora del partido. Hay victorias que se explican por el brillo del fútbol y otras que se ganan a base de paciencia, oficio y un instante de inspiración. La de la Cultural Leonesa este domingo en la segunda jornada del Grupo 1 de la Primera Federación pertenece a la segunda categoría. Un tanto de Pedro Benito en el minuto 65, servido en bandeja por Oier López, bastó para tumbar a un Mérida AD que se quedó con diez tras un partido áspero, marcado por las tarjetas y por la falta de puntería visitante ante la puerta. Final: 1-0. FICHA TÉCNICA Cultural Leonesa – 1: Parera; Iago López, Jaso, Jaime Vázquez, Oier López (Pomares, min. 83); Sergi Maestre (Algobia, min.65), Bicho (Jon García, min. 90+2); Pedro Benito (Hugo García, min. 90+2), Álex Cardero (Ndiaye, min. 83), Queipo; Jorge Delgado. AD Mérida – 0: Adrián Csenterics; Alejandro Jay, Nacho González, Hugo Carrillo (Koné, min.86), Barbu (Sofiane, min.73); Gio, Martín Solar (Guagua, min.86); Javi Areso, Beneit, Sandoval (Jota, min.62); Hallsson (Fito, min.73). Goles: 1-0, Pedro Benito, min.64. Árbitro: Álvaro Juncal (comité gallego). Mostró la cartulina amarilla a Jaso y a Bicho en la Cultural y a Carrillo y Nacho en el Mérida. Expulsó por doble amonestación a Gio. Estadio Reino de León (5.715 espectadores). Partido correspondiente a la 2ª jornada del grupo I de Primera RFEF. Un primer tiempo de fricción y cero goles El acta arbitral del primer acto habla por sí sola: cuatro amonestaciones antes del descanso, tres de ellas para el conjunto emeritense. Gio Almeida vio la primera amarilla ya en el minuto 14, un aviso temprano de por dónde iban a discurrir los acontecimientos. Le siguieron Hugo Carrillo (26') y Nacho González (39'), mientras que por la Cultural el veterano Bicho (39') también entró en el carrusel de tarjetas. El intermedio llegó con el marcador virgen (0-0), reflejo de dos equipos más preocupados por no conceder que por arriesgar. Benito rompe el nudo, el Mérida se queda con diez El choque necesitaba un chispazo y llegó tras la hora de juego. El técnico local había movido el banquillo un minuto antes: Ángel Algobia entró por Sergio Maestre en el 62'. Y en el 65', la jugada del partido. Oier López, uno de los futbolistas de mayor valor de la plantilla leonesa desde su posición de lateral, filtró el pase decisivo para que Pedro Benito definiera el 1-0. Fue el atacante madrileño, el jugador con mayor seguimiento de la alineación, quien firmó el gol que resolvería la tarde. El Mérida, obligado a estirarse, recibió el golpe definitivo apenas ocho minutos después. En el 73', Gio Almeida vio la segunda amarilla y, con ella, la roja que dejaba a los visitantes con diez hombres para el último cuarto de hora largo. Cuesta arriba y en inferioridad numérica, el conjunto extremeño perdió la fe pese a los refrescos ofensivos con Sofiane El Ftouhi, Darwin Guagua —el joven ecuatoriano de mayor valoración del mercado en el once visitante— y Lacine Kone. La Cultural, más ordenada con Carlos Pomares y Assane Ndiaye Dione en el campo, supo administrar la renta hasta el pitido final. Lo que dice la clasificación El triunfo tiene lectura inmediata en la tabla del Grupo 1. La Cultural Leonesa suma 4 puntos (una victoria y un empate en dos jornadas) y se instala en la octava plaza con un balance defensivo impecable: un gol a favor, ninguno en contra. Los de León todavía no saben lo que es encajar en este arranque liguero, un dato que refuerza la idea de un equipo construido sobre la solidez atrás y la efectividad de sus puntas. El Mérida AD, por su parte, se queda con 3 puntos (una victoria y una derrota) y cae hasta la duodécima posición. Su registro goleador —un tanto marcado, uno recibido— dibuja a un equipo competitivo pero al que le falta pegada para transformar el buen trabajo en resultados. La expulsión de Almeida, además, condiciona su planificación para la próxima jornada. En lo más alto del grupo mandan con paso firme Real Unión Club, Pontevedra CF y UD Logroñés, los tres con pleno de seis puntos. Por abajo, Real Avilés, Unión Deportiva Ourense y Unionistas de Salamanca CF siguen sin estrenar su casillero de puntos. Los protagonistas El nombre de la tarde es Pedro Benito. Su gol en el 65' no solo decidió el partido, sino que confirma su papel de referencia ofensiva en el proyecto leonés. Fue relevado en el minuto 90 por Jon García, ya con la faena hecha. Merece mención Oier López, autor de la asistencia y uno de los jugadores más determinantes por su banda, retirado en el 82' entre aplausos tras dejar su sello en la acción clave. Y en portería, Miquel Parera mantuvo su marco a cero, prolongando la muralla defensiva que exhibe la Cultural en este inicio de campeonato. Por el Mérida, el capítulo lo protagoniza en negativo Gio Almeida: dos amarillas y una expulsión que dejó a su equipo sin margen de reacción. El guardameta húngaro Adrián Csenterics, pese a la derrota, evitó un resultado más abultado. Conclusión Fue una victoria de las que valen doble en una categoría tan igualada: sin encajar, con un solo disparo transformado en oro y sabiendo sufrir con diez rivales por delante. La Cultural Leonesa se marcha del Grupo 1 con la sensación de haber encontrado ya su identidad —orden atrás, eficacia arriba— mientras el Mérida AD deberá corregir su indisciplina y afinar la puntería si quiere escalar posiciones. En la Primera Federación, donde los detalles lo deciden todo, la tarde en el Reino de León se resolvió en un pase de Oier y un remate de Benito.

articles.title: NBC says its cameras 'are not the official arbiter of timekeeping' after officials added 1 second back for Michigan's miracle Hail Mary
articles.summary: The Big Ten released a video late Saturday night showing there was a second remaining on the game clock on Michigan's first Hail Mary attempt.
articles.body:
NBC made it clear on Sunday afternoon that its clock is not the official game clock during Big Ten games.

No. 16 Michigan shocked Western Michigan 13-12 on an Hail Mary as time expired after officials added one second back to the clock following an initial Hail Mary attempt that fell incomplete as time seemingly expired.

NBC's replays showed immediately after the play that the game clock was at 0:00 when Western Michigan's Micah Davis touched the ball after stepping out of bounds before jumping. However, the Big Ten's official game clock showed one second left on the clock at the time that Davis touched the ball.

"The official time of the game is kept by the Big Ten. Our cameras are not the official arbiter of timekeeping within the game," said a statement from NBC announcer John Fanta during halftime of Washington vs. Washington State. "That is the Big Ten and game officials' responsibility. After the game last night, the Big Ten released a statement and raw video from its replay process that showed how and why the decision was made."

The possible clock sync issue was immediately pointed out by NBC's rules analyst Terry McAuley. He said it was the only possible explanation for the conference adding a second back to the clock as the clock on NBC's screen showed 0:00 when the play ended.

It's possible that NBC's clock started a fraction of a second too early on the penultimate play of the game. After a 28-yard completion with 11 seconds to go, Michigan hurried to the line and spiked the ball. That play took two seconds, and the referee requested over the stadium microphone for the clock operator to set the game clock at nine seconds.

At the time of the announcement, NBC's ticker showed eight seconds to go. That clock was reset to nine seconds, but it quickly ticked back to eight seconds as the ball hit Underwood's hands on the shotgun snap for the incomplete Hail Mary. That potential time difference could be more than enough to make up for the fraction of a second that elapsed between the clock that NBC showed hitting 0:00 before the ball traveled a few more feet toward Davis.

Sunday afternoon, Western Michigan president Russ Kavalhuna and coach Lance Taylor held a news conference to say they accepted the outcome of the game and that they were looking to make the best of what has been a bitter moment. Taylor emphasized that the officials "did not cost [us] the game."

"It's not what happens to you, it's how you respond that ultimately determines success or failure," Taylor said.
